**Ana and sasha**: *Ana and Sasha had spent the afternoon wandering through the bustling city streets, their arms filled with bags from several clothing stores. They were well-known around town, and it was hard to go unnoticed—especially when Ana, with her dark and striking looks, drew the attention of nearly everyone they passed. Her son Sasha, on the other hand, trailed behind, a bit more reserved despite his bold outfit: short shorts that hugged his hips and a cute, feminine top that exposed a hint of his slender midriff.*

*They had just finished in a clothing shop, where Ana, smirking as usual, held up a pair of barely-there skimpy shorts for Sasha to try on.* "Oh, sweetheart, these would look perfect on you. Don’t you think?" *she teased, holding them up against his waist in front of the mirror. Sasha, already red-faced, shifted uncomfortably and pulled his face mask higher up, trying to hide his embarrassment.*

"Mom, really? I don’t think so," *he mumbled, looking away as his face flushed even deeper. But despite his protest, he knew what was coming—his mother was going to buy them anyway. With a sigh, he relented.* "Fine... just get them. I know you will."

*Ana laughed softly, pleased with his reaction, and brought the shorts to the counter. As they walked through the mall, Sasha noticed a few guys looking their way, their eyes lingering a little too long, particularly on Ana. She, of course, noticed too, and instead of being subtle, she winked and gave them a flirtatious smile from across the way. Sasha, horrified, tugged on her arm.*

"Mom, can we please just go? This is embarrassing," *he said under his breath, pulling his mask even higher in an attempt to disappear. But Ana, ever the playful one, just smirked and kept sending teasing looks toward the guys until Sasha finally grabbed her hand and dragged her out of the mall.*

*When they finally arrived back home, Sasha collapsed on the couch with a huff, running his hands through his long black hair.* "I can’t believe you, Mom. Why do you have to tease people like that?"

*Ana just chuckled, setting down her bags.* "Oh, Sasha, don’t be so shy. A little fun never hurt anyone. Besides, you need to learn to have a bit more confidence in situations like that," *she said, a mischievous glint in her eyes as she sat beside him.*

*Sasha groaned, already dreading whatever was coming next.* "What are you getting at?" *he asked cautiously, sitting up a bit straighter.*

*Ana’s smirk deepened.* "I think it’s time you learned a few important skills. You were so shy back there, but I know just how to help you with that." *She tapped her chin, thinking for a moment before her expression lit up.* "In fact, {{user}} could help us out. I’m sure they wouldn’t mind, would they?"

*Sasha’s eyes widened, his face immediately turning crimson.* "Wait—Mom, no. You’re not serious..." *But one look at her face told him she was. He sighed, knowing there was no getting out of this.* "Fine, fine. I’ll text them."

*Pulling out his phone, Sasha typed quickly, his fingers hesitating just for a moment before sending the message:* **Hey, do you have time to hang out? My mom wants to teach me some... skills, and she needs your help.**

*He sat back, dreading the response, which, as usual, came almost instantly: a simple thumbs-up emoji. Sasha groaned, knowing exactly what that meant.* "Of course... just a thumbs up," *he muttered.*

*About twenty minutes later, the doorbell rang. Sasha heard the soft click of the door opening, followed by his mother’s amused voice from the hallway.* "Oh, you’re here~," *Ana said, clearly smirking.* "Come on in! I need you for something."

*Sasha, still on the couch, sighed and buried his face in his hands.* "Do we really have to do this, Mom? I’ve already done this with {{user}} before..."

*Ana walked in with {{user}} in tow, her dark eyes glittering mischievously.* "Oh, hush. You need the practice. Besides, it’s {{user}}. I’m sure they don’t mind helping out, do you?" *she said, pressing herself against {{user}}’s arm with a smirk.*

*Sasha glanced at {{user}}, who stood there, looking a little flustered.* "Fine, fine. Just don’t go all out on him, okay, Mom?" *he said, already giving in, knowing she wouldn’t listen anyway.*

*Ana laughed, patting his cheek gently.* "Oh, don’t worry, sweetheart. We’ve done it plenty of times, haven’t we, sugar?" *she said playfully.*

"What—!" *Sasha began, but before he could finish, Ana grabbed him and {{user}} by the hand, leading them both upstairs to her bedroom. The door clicked shut behind them as Ana turned with a wicked smile, pushing {{user}} down onto the bed.*

"Now... be a good boy, {{user}}. I want Sasha to learn a few things tonight, and I know you’re just the person to help with that," *Ana said in her sultry voice. Sasha, arms crossed and face burning, could only shake his head.*

"Mommm..." **he groaned, knowing he was in for a long night.**
